title: Induction Coiler
pages: Craft the controller in a 3x3 grid. Top row: lightning rod, silver ingot (forge:ingots/silver), lightning rod. Middle row: copper ingot, Insulated Pulse Contact (electrolyze purified salts for its Conductive Crystal core), fired Brazed Joint. Bottom row: Crimp Press-made crimped collar, Smoke Rack-made Creosote Lagging, crimped collar. Smoke white wool in a lit rack to impregnate its fibre with tar; the treated wrap thermally isolates the windings, while raw wool and planks cannot replace it. Place a lightning rod directly beneath it, glass directly above it, and redstone lamps on all four horizontal sides. Any missing or swapped side, cap or base stops operation. Stamp one light weighted pressure plate (two silver ingots) into two Stamped Silver Contacts in the Press (100 ticks, 8 FE/t), then assemble them around a Conductive Crystal with two copper leads, a fired Porcelain Insulator and a Crimp Press-made collar. The collar retains the contact stack under compression; the porcelain keeps the pulse path off the chassis. The Drawing Bench spring belongs to the later Solenoid route and cannot gate this earlier coiler. A bare crystal or contact blank cannot replace the assembly. For the Brazed Joint, craft two Prepared Braze Joints from two copper ingots, two silver ingots and blaze powder, then heat each in a Clinker Oven for 200 ticks at 12 FE/t. The fired silver-copper seam joins the coil contact; bare copper and the unfired lap cannot substitute.

Right-click the formed controller with feedstock from a loaded induction winding recipe to load it into the stock buffer; nothing comes out instantly. Each batch runs for the recipe's duration and draws its FE every tick: 100 ticks at 20 FE/t by default, 160 ticks at 32 FE/t for the Wound Coil. Without FE the batch stalls with status no_power and keeps its progress; a missing cap, base or lamp pauses processing and resets progress without consuming stock. Feed FE through a Stock Hatch that replaces a frame part (the controller holds 16,000 FE). For automation, insert valid winding stock into the controller from any face except the bottom and extract products from the bottom; reach these covered faces through Stock Hatches. The controller buffers one input stack and one output stack, saves both with its stored FE and face modes, and exposes Forge item handlers to hoppers or pipes; stock with no winding recipe is refused. Sneak-right-click with an empty hand to cycle the clicked face through input, output and disabled. Right-click with an empty hand to collect buffered output.

It runs 21 exclusive datapack induction_winding recipes. Nineteen take two raw ore chunks (tin, lead, zinc, nickel, silver, cobalt, platinum, iridium, aluminum, tungsten, bismuth, manganese, antimony, chromium, titanium, molybdenum, vanadium, niobium, tantalum) and wind out three matching ingots with no furnace or fuel, a faster no-fuel alternative to smelting for players automating large batches. The twentieth winds three conductive crystals into a Wound Coil. The twenty-first anneals one Drawn Iron Rod from the Wire Drawing Bench into a Soft-Iron Plunger: the coil heats the cold-worked rod by induction, restoring the soft magnetic iron a Solenoid plunger needs (temperature and soak time are abstracted). With JEI installed, search the Induction Coiler controller to see every loaded recipe, batch count and formation requirement.

A Wound Coil replaces one sealed steel plate corner in the Resonance Infuser's crafting grid. Two more coils, a Drive Shaft, two Sintered Bronze Bushings and iron ingots make a Wound Motor for the Magnetizer controller. The Capacitor Array and Magnetizer later claim two more Infuser corners, leaving one plain plate. A Wound Coil, a Soft-Iron Plunger, four iron ingots and a Coil Spring also make the Solenoid that the Spectral Loom controller needs. This is the second required t4 apparatus; a plain plate in that corner no longer completes the craft. The centre Insulated Pulse Contact is the coil pulse switch; stamp its silver faces in a powered Press and keep the Porcelain Insulator fired before assembly.

Stock Hatches: every face of this controller is covered by a frame part, so hoppers and pipes reach it through Stock Hatches. Place a hatch instead of any part that touches the controller face-to-face; at most two hatches may stand in, and a third breaks formation. A hatch relays only while the frame is formed, and it relays the controller face it covers: insert stock into a hatch on an In face, and extract products from a hatch whose face you sneak-use with an empty hand to cycle to Out (the base face starts as Out). For example, swap one side part for a hatch fed by a hopper pointing into it from beside, and swap the base part for a hatch with a hopper beneath it. A hopper touching a redstone block or other powered part is locked by vanilla rules. Right-clicking a hatch with an empty hand collects the product buffer. Hatches also relay Forge Energy into this powered controller, so a cable or generator touching a hatch keeps it running.
